history.origins: Truco is descended from the simpler game Truc (Truque), which originated in parts of Spain (Valencia, Balearic Islands) and Southern France. It spread to South America with colonization and became the national card game of Argentina, with distinct regional forms in Uruguay, Brazil, Chile, and Venezuela. The bluffing, talking, and joking that accompany play are an integral part of its cultural role.
timeline: Truc from Valencia and Balearic Islands; Truco spread in South America and became Argentina's national game.

setup.deck: 40 Spanish cards (no 8s, 9s, 10s). Special ranking: Aâ™  > Aâ™£ > 7â™  > 7â™¦ > 3s > 2s > False As > 12s > 11s > 10s > False 7s > 6s > 5s > 4s.
setup.dealing: Each player is dealt three cards from the 40-card deck; no further cards are drawn during play. The deal rotates counterclockwise; the player to the right of the dealer (mano) plays first, the dealer (pie) plays last.

rules.objective: The objective is to be the first team to reach 30 points. Points are split into two halves: the lower half (malas, 1 to 15) and the higher half (buenas, 16 to 30); the first team to complete 30 points wins the game.
rules.gameplay: Win 2/3 tricks. Three lances: 1) ENVIDO (2 same-suit values + 20, higher wins, 2 pts). 2) TRUCO (raise trick value: Truco=2, Retruco=3, Vale Cuatro=4). 3) FLOR (3 same suit, 3 pts, cancels Envido). Respond Quiero/No Quiero. Massive bluffing.

strategy.basic: Bluff with weak hands. Don't concede easily.
strategy.intermediate: Coordinate signals with partner. Time Envido calls.
